title: Adaptation of Brief Resilient Coping Scale (BRCS) to Brazilian Portuguese
abstract: This study aimed to adapt and validate the Brief Resilient Coping Scale (BRCS) for a sample of Brazilian adults. The adaptation process included translation and expert analysis using the three-stage Delphi technique. A total of 698 Brazilian adults, with a mean age of 48.4 years ( SD = 15.3), of whom 79% were women, completed the BRCS. To examine construct validity, confirmatory factor analyses and correlation analyses with indicators of depression, anxiety, and stress were conducted. The one-dimensional theoretical model demonstrated good fit (CFI = .998, TLI = .994, RMSEA = .058 [.017, .107], SRMR = .023), albeit not perfect, χ 2 (2) = 7.177, p = .028. The factor loadings were all above .30, varying from .62 to .82. The correlations between BRCS and the DASS-8 subscales were significant with p < .001 and r = -.31 for the correlation with depression, -.28 for anxiety and -.26 for stress. In comparison to previous studies of validity evidence of BRCS, our results presented the best values indicating suitability for Brazilian context. For that, we consider the BRCS to be a valid and reliable instrument for assessing resilient coping in the Brazilian population.
